h1: The 7 Best Small Toaster Ovens for Tight Counters, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Toaster Ovens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 small toaster ovens compared on capacity, slice count, power, air fry and build, from the Dash Mini to Breville smart ovens.
summary: The Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven is the small toaster oven to buy if you want a compact box that cooks properly, not just browns bread. The Breville BOV680BSS adds air fry to a compact body, the Elite Gourmet ETO490 is the best budget four-slice, and the Dash Mini is the cheapest way to get a toaster oven into a dorm room.
intro: The slice count on the box is the number everyone reads and the one that misleads most. A four-slice rating tells you how many pieces of bread fit side by side, not whether a small frozen pizza, a muffin tin or a cookie sheet will go in. A small oven should be judged by what you cook, and the interior width and height are the dimensions that decide that.

So we ranked these seven by how much real cooking they handle in a small footprint. We reviewed the listings for slice count, litre capacity, wattage, air fry, pizza settings, build material and price bracket, from under $25 to the $200 to $500 range. Some listings omit key numbers, and where they do we say so.

products.name: Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven
products.verdict: The mini smart oven that cooks like a bigger one, in a stainless body.
products.description:
The BOV450XL is a stainless steel mini oven from Breville's smart oven line, sold in the $100 to $200 range. Where the cheaper boxes are simple on and off elements, this one is built around controlled heating and a more deliberate design.

That is the reason it leads. A small oven's biggest weakness is uneven heat, since a short cavity puts food close to the elements and burns tops before centres cook. Smart control helps manage that, and the metal shell gives the appliance a sturdier feel than painted-plastic rivals. It ranks above the BOV680BSS because it does the core jobs with fewer moving parts, even though it lacks air fry.

Buy it if you want one small oven to do toast, reheats and small bakes well. The caveat is that the listing does not give the interior dimensions, so measure your favourite tray before you order.
products.idealFor: People who want a small oven that cooks properly.
products.skipIf: You only toast bread and want the cheapest unit.

products.name: Breville BOV680BSS Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact
products.verdict: A compact Breville smart oven that adds an air fry mode to the formula.
products.description:
The BOV680BSS is a compact smart oven with an air fry function, sold in the $200 to $500 range, the highest bracket in this ranking. It folds an air fryer's crisping ability into a body meant for a small counter.

Air fry changes what a small oven can do. Frozen fries, wings and roasted vegetables come out crisp rather than soft, so you can retire a separate basket-style air fryer. It sits second, behind the BOV450XL, purely because of price: the extra money buys convenience, not better toast, and the listing gives no capacity figure to compare against the cheaper boxes.

Buy it if you want to replace both a toaster oven and an air fryer in one purchase. Skip it if you never fry frozen food and the mini model already covers your cooking.
pros: Air fry in a compact body
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want oven and air fryer in one.
products.skipIf: You never cook frozen or fried food.

products.name: Breville BOV650XL Compact Smart Oven
products.verdict: A roomier stainless smart oven for households that outgrow the mini.
products.description:
The BOV650XL is a stainless steel compact smart oven priced in the $100 to $200 range, one size up from the mini. It keeps the sturdy shell and the controlled heating, with more space inside.

More space is the point. A bigger tray means a whole meal fits, so you stop cooking in two rounds. It ranks third because it is no longer truly small by countertop standards, and anyone short of room may find it dominates the surface. The listing again omits dimensions, so measure your gap and the cabinets above it before committing.

Buy it if you cook for two to four and want a countertop oven to do most of the work. Skip it if your priority is the smallest possible footprint.
pros: More interior room than the mini
products.idealFor: Households of two to four wanting one capable oven.
products.skipIf: You need the smallest possible footprint.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO490 9L/4-Slice Oven
products.verdict: A 9 litre, four-slice oven that gives real space for the $25 to $50 range.
products.description:
The ETO490 offers a 9 litre cavity and four-slice capacity, in the $25 to $50 range. Nine litres is a useful figure because it is a volume, and it lets you compare directly with other ovens that state litres.

It lands fourth because it delivers the size that matters most at a fraction of the Breville price. That is enough for toast, bagels, a small pizza or a pair of chicken thighs. What it does not offer is smart heating or a metal shell, and basic ovens in this class tend to brown unevenly near the elements. The listing also leaves out wattage.

Buy it if you want the most capacity per dollar. Skip it if you expect the even results of a Breville.
products.idealFor: Budget cooks who want the most space per dollar.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO449X Toaster Oven
products.verdict: Four slices, 800 watts, 8.99 litres and a pizza function for $25 to $50.
products.description:
The ETO449X lists four-slice capacity, 800 watts, an 8.99 litre cavity and a pizza function, in the $25 to $50 range. It is the only oven in the group that states both a wattage and a litre figure.

That transparency helps with comparison. Next to the ETO490 it is slightly smaller, but you gain a defined power rating and a pizza setting that suits frozen pies. The 800 watt rating means it takes a little longer to come up to heat than stronger ovens, which is the usual cost of a low-power small box. It ranks below the ETO490 because the capacity is a shade lower and both are otherwise similar.

Buy it if you want a pizza button and published power. Skip it if you need the biggest cavity at this price.
products.idealFor: Frozen pizza fans on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want the biggest cavity possible.

products.name: Dash Mini Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The smallest and cheapest oven here, with a pizza function, for under $25.
products.description:
The Dash Mini Toaster Oven is priced under $25 and lists a pizza function. As the name says, it is the most compact option in this ranking, built for dorm shelves and desks.

Its size is the whole appeal. It heats quickly, uses little counter space and handles toast, a single bagel, a snack-size pizza or a quesadilla. It ranks sixth because the listing gives no capacity, wattage or slice figures, and mini ovens at this price usually trade finish and control for cost. You should expect basic dial controls and a single small tray.

Buy it if space and price outrank everything else. Skip it if you want to cook anything bigger than a snack.
products.idealFor: Dorm rooms and desks where space is scarce.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO236 Compact 2-Slice Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A two-slice compact oven for the smallest kitchens, in the $25 to $50 range.
products.description:
The ETO236 is a compact two-slice toaster oven in the $25 to $50 range. Two slices is the smallest official capacity in the ranking, aimed at one-person kitchens and secondary spaces such as a camper or an office.

A two-slice oven does one thing well, which is toast and reheats for a single person. It ranks last because it offers less than the Dash Mini at a higher price bracket, and the listing gives no wattage, litre or function details. The brand's other ovens give more room for the same money, so choose this one only if its footprint is the deciding factor.

Buy it if you need a very small, plain oven for a single person. Skip it if you might host guests or cook for two.

whatMatters.detail: Slice count tells you how much bread fits, but trays, pans and pizzas are set by interior width, depth and height. A litre figure such as the 9 L of the ETO490 is easier to compare. Measure your usual pan and look for interior dimensions on the listing.

Small ovens run from modest wattage, and the figure sets how quickly they climb to temperature. The 800 watts on the ETO449X is gentle on the circuit but slower than a stronger oven. Check that the listing states wattage rather than leaving it blank.

A small cavity puts food close to the elements, which can burn tops before the middle cooks. Smart control and good airflow help. Look for the words smart oven, convection or air fry, and be wary of basic on and off elements for anything beyond toast.

Air fry adds crisp results and can replace a second appliance, while a pizza setting just tunes the heat for frozen pies. Decide which job you do most often. If it is toast and reheats, presets are enough.

Stainless shells feel sturdier and hold heat better than thin plastic. Footprint matters for fit under cabinets and for the clearance around the oven. Allow space on all sides, because small ovens still get hot on the outside.

faq.q: Will a small toaster oven fit a standard pizza?
faq.a: A frozen personal pizza usually fits, but a 12 inch pie does not. Measure the interior width on the listing, and remember that heating elements sit close to the food in small ovens.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a small toaster oven?
faq.a: Buying by slice count alone. Two ovens with the same slice rating can differ in height and depth, which decides whether a baking dish fits. Compare litres or interior dimensions.

faq.q: Is the Breville BOV450XL worth it over the Elite Gourmet ETO490?
faq.a: If you use it daily, yes. The Breville offers more even heating and a sturdier shell, while the ETO490 gives more raw capacity for far less money.

faq.q: How much clearance does a toaster oven need?
faq.a: Leave several inches of open space on the sides and above, and keep it off paper or plastic. The outer surface gets hot, even on small units.

faq.q: How do I clean the inside?
faq.a: Unplug it, let it cool, empty the crumb tray, and wipe the walls with a damp cloth and mild soap. Avoid soaking the unit or using harsh scouring pads.

faq.q: Can I bake in a small toaster oven?
faq.a: Yes, in small trays. Use a pan that clears the elements by at least an inch, and watch the first batch, since small ovens often run hotter at the top than the dial suggests.

finalTake: For most kitchens, the Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven is the best small toaster oven here: controlled heating and a stainless build in a compact body. Step up to the BOV680BSS for air fry, or choose the BOV650XL for bigger meals. On a budget, the Elite Gourmet ETO490 offers the most space for the money, and the Dash Mini is the dorm answer. Measure your tray before you order, because slice count is not the same as usable space.
